subject: Edge streaming qualification & geo-residency follow-up
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@helioshealth.com>, Priya Das <priya.d@helioshealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Edge streaming qualification & geo-residency follow-up

Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap + a few clarifying questions so we can scope a focused perf validation run next week. I pulled the numbers we discussed into the attached perf_matrix.xlsx and annotated a suggested 3-phase test plan. Please confirm the items below so we can align the test harness and the Dedicated pool sizing.

Key asks / notes from our call:
- Latency SLOs: target P95 token latency of 200–350ms for typical chat flows; want explicit targets per region (US / EU / APAC).
- Streaming: you require server-sent event streaming with per-token flushes (low-latency streaming) and graceful reconnection behavior.
- Throughput & concurrency: expected steady-state 1,200 qps with bursts up to 6,000 qps; ~8,000 concurrent active sessions during peak.
- Data residency: EU customer data must remain in eu-central-1 for storage and inference paths; APAC traffic should remain in ap-southeast-1 where possible.
- Failover: acceptable to route to a nearby region for up to 60s for retries, but any data written to EU storage must stay in EU.

Questions for you (please confirm in reply):
1) Are the throughput and concurrency numbers above representative of your 95th percentile peak, or are those absolute maxima?
2) Is EU residency required for all data types (including telemetry/token-level traces), or only for PHI and storage-at-rest?
3) For APAC latency targets: do you have a P95 target for whole-response latency (end-to-end) vs. per-token latency?

Next steps we propose once you confirm:
- Redwood will provision a temporary dedicated pool in ap-southeast-1 and eu-central-1 for a 48-hour soak.
- We'll run a 3-phase test (baseline, soak, failover) and share raw metrics + a trimmed report.

Attachments: perf_matrix.xlsx (model sizing & preliminary throughput estimates).

Thanks — I’ll schedule the short technical deep-dive with our infra lead once we get your confirmations.

—
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.com

From: Samir Patel <samir@helioshealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Das <priya.d@helioshealth.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Edge streaming qualification & geo-residency follow-up

Sofia — thanks for the recap and the rapid turnaround. A few clarifications below:

- Throughput / concurrency: the numbers I gave were conservative maxima during a product launch. For steady-state planning, assume 1,000 qps and ~2,500 concurrent active sessions; launch-day bursts could approach 8,000 concurrent.
- EU residency: must apply to all persisted user data and any PII/PHI. Telemetry for performance can be sampled, but full request/response payloads must not leave the EU when tagged as EU.
- APAC targets: we'd like P95 end-to-end response time (from client request to final token) under 500ms for APAC customers. Per-token latency is useful for ops tuning, but the business requirement is end-to-end P95.

One operational ask: can Redwood provide a brief SOC2 summary document and example audit-log extract fields so our security/compliance team can triage? Also please include notes on automatic fallback routing behavior if ap-southeast-1 becomes unavailable.

If you can provision a short proof-of-performance next week that exercises the APAC pool and demonstrates residency, that would be ideal.

Thanks —
Samir Patel
Head of Platform Engineering, Helios Health
samir@helioshealth.com

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@helioshealth.com>, Priya Das <priya.d@helioshealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 07:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Edge streaming qualification & geo-residency follow-up

Samir — appreciate the clarity, this helps a lot. Quick answers and an operational proposal below.

Residency / telemetry:
- We can ensure persisted request/response payloads and user profile storage for EU-tagged data remain in eu-central-1.
- Telemetry: by default we sample traces; for compliance we can enable full request logging for EU-tagged requests stored in EU buckets (audit-log extract attached).
- SOC2: attaching a short SOC2 summary (redwood-soc2-summary.pdf).

Latency & routing strategy:
- Routing: client IP geolocation -> preferred region routing (ap-southeast-1 / eu-central-1 / us-east-1).
- Fallback behavior: if preferred region reports degraded healthy capacity, traffic will failover to the next region (configurable threshold). For EU-persisted payloads we will still route processing in EU, but if EU compute is unavailable we will queue writes to EU storage and process in a nearby region for read-only or cached responses only (we'll document acceptable failure modes).

Performance expectations (for your model family):
- Dedicated single-GPU pool (A100 80GB equiv) with quantized weights: ~900–1,300 qps steady depending on sample length and batching; P95 per-token latency in-region typically 80–220ms with continuous streaming enabled.
- For end-to-end P95 (what you asked for): with an ap-southeast-1 colocated pool and client-edge routing we expect ~300–500ms for APAC depending on client network. We will instrument end-to-end tests to show both per-token and whole-response P95.
- Burst capacity: we recommend a small reserved buffer (20–30% capacity) plus autoscale policy to handle launch spikes; we can provision temporary burst nodes for the launch window.

Test plan (short):
1) Baseline: 2 hours steady 1,000 qps from APAC endpoints, collect per-token + end-to-end P95.
2) Soak: 6 hours at 1,200–2,000 qps to validate stability and KV cache behavior.
3) Failover: controlled region outage simulation to validate fallbacks and EU-residency guarantees.

Next asks for you: confirm that EU persistence applies to request payloads and logs (yes/no), and confirm one preferred week for the validation run (we have 28–30 Jun and 5–7 Jul windows available).

Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf, (audit-log-extract.csv - sample fields shown inline).

—
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.com
